scoreNotes: Comparative evidence against the original and fixed target, not a numeric approval threshold. The sole blocker is the repeatable E/W cap-edge RGB discontinuity.
observations: The original half-post construction, sag, cap and two bindings per post remain recognizable and registered. The candidate visibly improves the source: cap tops have soft low-contrast ring/form shading rather than flat lemon plates, bodies remain warm amber, and the cream rope now shows a gentle top/front/underside value change.

At logical 192 x 352 size, N/E/S/W have coherent soft cartoon materials. The warmer, quieter highlights avoid the target halo, wet gloss, strongly inflated blocks and extra grain. Near E/W cut faces remain flat authored modular planes; these are accepted intentional boundaries.

N/S independent three-module alpha-over joins reconstruct full caps/posts/bindings without an evident vertical split, gap, doubled ridge or rope separation. The open outer partial posts remain available for inspection.

E/W independent joins have complete alpha coverage, but a faint straight horizontal color line crosses both internal cap tops at native preview rows y=484 and y=740. It repeats across the cap diameter in joined-independent-E.png and joined-independent-W.png and is absent from the matching joined-native images. Enlarged crops reveal a surface bisector rather than an organic growth ring; the line is faint at logical size but persists on both repeated post tops.

Inspected all four full-frame native renders and every packet preview directly. Also inspected verified logical-size/background composites and 4x nearest cap-edge crops made from the exact hashed files. No large dead spots, black wedges, floating rope, directional ground cast shadow, glow halo or new frame clipping were found elsewhere.

blockers.location: joined-independent-E.png and joined-independent-W.png: both internal full cap tops, centered about x=576 at y=484 and y=740 in the 1152 x 1216 native assembly frame; compare joined-native-E.png / joined-native-W.png.
blockers.effect: A repeatable thin straight darker/warmer bisector reveals the split between independently captured cap halves even though alpha is opaque. It interrupts the soft continuous cap surface and fails the frozen joined-continuity outcome. This is subtle, but it recurs at every E/W internal post and is not present in the native assembled context.
blockers.desiredVisibleOutcome: Independent E/W native sprite assembly should retain the same continuous cap ring/color impression as the joined mesh context, with no straight shared-edge stripe at native or logical size. Preserve exact geometry, port planes, registration, rotation convention and general warm soft treatment.
blockers.evidence: Visual inspection of actual independent/native images, light-background comparisons, honest logical-size assembly views, and enlarged unaltered-pixel crops. Supporting samples across x=541..610 show alpha 255 and mean independent-minus-native RGB near [-2.5,-3.5,-5.0] at row 484 and [-2.4,-3.6,-5.6] at row 740; these numbers support the visible seam rather than substituting for inspection.

remainingDifferences: The native model keeps the original lightly segmented rope and faceted outlines rather than copying the target inflated pillowy segments.
Wood grain is much more restrained than the target; the broad low-contrast cap rings and amber body shading are sufficient for the chosen cartoon treatment at logical size.
The original half-post boundary faces, cap thickness and frame padding remain intact. They intentionally differ from imagegen silhouette and composition drift.
